Subject: Performance SLO & context window follow-up (FinCo)

Thanks for the call today — great conversation. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we keep momentum.

Recap (from our notes):
- Business SLO: customer-facing assistant must feel real-time for short interactions; target p95 <= 200-250ms for typical prompts (<=512 tokens).
- Context window: you indicated up to ~8k tokens of historical context for some flows, plus outputs up to ~2k tokens for longer explanations.
- Streaming: streaming output is required for the user experience on the product side, especially for longer responses.
- Throughput/concurrency: initial launch expected ~30 concurrent active users during peak, target sustained throughput ~50 req/s with burst to 150 req/s.
- Compliance/Procurement: procurement will want draft SLA and perf numbers before term sheet — attached a perf summary and a starter SLA (redwood_perf_sheet.xlsx, SLA-draft-finco.docx).

Open questions / asks (please reply inline):
1) Can you confirm the typical request size distribution (percent of requests at <=512, 512-2048, 2048-8192 tokens)?
2) For streaming, do you need chunked responses for both partial completions and incremental token streaming, or just streaming on final answer?
3) Any hard p50/p95 targets for the 8k-context scenarios we should use for capacity planning?
4) Who should join an engineering deep-dive next week (names + availability)?

Next steps I propose:
- Dev/Eng call to go over perf targets + sample payloads (can you share a representative payload for the 8k flow?)
- We'll run an initial benchmark on dedicated capacity and share p50/p95 numbers for the three request-size buckets by EOW next week.
- We'll update the SLA draft based on the agreed targets.

Attachments: redwood_perf_sheet.xlsx (summary of measured p50/p95 across model variants), SLA-draft-finco.docx (starter language).

Thanks — happy to coordinate times.
\Cheers,

Subject: Re: Performance SLO & context window follow-up (FinCo)

Liam — perfect, thanks for the distribution and clarity on streaming. Short follow-up with more detail on tradeoffs and what we'll benchmark.
\High level notes (what we expect and what we'll measure):
- Context window impact: latency grows with input length primarily because of attention and KV-cache management. For the same model on our serving runtime, we typically see:~
  - <=512 tokens: p95 in the 120-220ms range on a typical generation (model-dependent)
  - 2048 tokens: p95 increases to ~350-450ms for non-streaming completions
  - 8k tokens: p95 can be 700ms-1.2s for non-streaming, depending on output length and model variant.
- Streaming effect: enabling streaming reduces perceived latency (tokens arrive earlier) and often reduces measured p50/p95 for first-byte latency by ~30-60% for long outputs — but total end-to-end work remains. We'll measure both first-byte and final-token latencies.
- Throughput & concurrency: batching improves throughput but can add queueing latency. For your target sustained 50 req/s with occasional bursts to 150 req/s, we'll test: 50 qps, 100 qps, 150 qps with concurrency levels of 30, 75, 200 respectively to see queuing behavior.
- Recommended baseline config for the benchmark:
  - Model variant: redwood-8k-encoder-q4 (quantized) and a higher-fidelity variant for comparison (redwood-16k-fp16)
  - Serving mode: Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) for predictable p95; we can run a hosted benchmark but dedicated will show production SLOs more reliably.
\Next steps / asks from you before the benchmark:
1) Share the sample payload (we saw the note that you have one — please upload to the shared Drive link).
2) Confirm which models you want us to test (we'll run our default open-model family if you don't specify).
3) Confirm the definition of success for the 8k bucket (is p95 <=800ms acceptable for initial launch?).
\I've updated the perf spreadsheet and placed a link to a suggested benchmark matrix in the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1FinCo-Perf-SLOs. We'll attach the raw logs and dashboards after runs.
\Proposed time for the deep-dive — Wed 6/9 10am PT works for us. I'll send a calendar invite with a short agenda and include our infra lead (Dev).
\Thanks — we'll prepare the initial benchmark and SLA updates.
\Best,
Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & context window follow-up (FinCo) — internal test plan
\Marissa / Dylan — quick internal note ahead of the Wed deep-dive. Proposed technical benchmark plan and things to capture.
\Proposed benchmark scenarios (we'll run each at 3 load points):
A) Short prompts: 256 input / 128 output, streaming on/off
B) Mid prompts: 2048 input / 512 output, streaming on/off
C) Long context: 8192 input / 2048 output, streaming on/off
\Load points: 50 qps sustained, 100 qps sustained, 150 qps burst (10s windows).
\Metrics to capture for each run:
- First-byte latency (stream start) and final-token latency (end-to-end), p50/p95/p99
- Per-request token counts and compute time breakdown (attention vs decoding)
- Queueing time due to batching and effective batch sizes seen by the runtime
- Memory / GPU utilization and any OOM events
\Acceptance targets to propose to FinCo in the SLA (we can be flexible but start conservative):
- Short (<=512): p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 400ms
- Mid (512-2048): p95 <= 500ms, p99 <= 900ms
- Long (8k context): p95 <= 900ms, p99 <= 1.5s
\Notes for the call: streaming will give them a better user perceived latency — so we should present both first-byte streaming numbers and end-to-end non-streaming numbers. Also explain tradeoffs around batching: at 150 qps bursts we will likely see larger batch sizes and higher p95 unless we cap max batch latency; propose a service-level cap of X ms for batching (we'll pick 12ms as an example cap to keep tail latency predictable).
\I'll spin up the test harness and allocate a dedicated benchmark pool. Please confirm the sample payload from FinCo when they upload it to the Drive folder so I can parameterize the requests.
\Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com
